column15: Verified via producer's own site (Hood River Distillers, Oregon): Lewis and Clark is a spirits line including Northwest Bourbon (Kentucky bourbon finished with Oregon oak, described on-site as "blended bourbon") and a Straight Corn Whiskey, plus non-whiskey spirits (vodka, gin, rum). Corrects seed's low-confidence country guess to a verified US/Oregon producer. defaultTypeName left empty since the row spans bourbon and corn whiskey. Peat=none per American whiskey norm; no smoke/peat mentioned on site.

Verified via producer's own site (Brave New Spirits): Lighthouse is a blended Scotch whisky with two expressions, Unpeated (baseline, this row) and Lightly Peated. The Lightly Peated expression is a distinct sibling profile expected to be caught by the KB's existing global "lightly peated" keyword rule (it literally contains the word "peat"), so no producer-specific rule.tsv row was added. This row represents the unpeated baseline.

Verified via producer's own site: Bardstown, KY distillery owned by Luxco, producing Rebel Bourbon, Ezra Brooks (see ezra-brooks, already live), Daviess County, Lux Row Double Barrel, David Nicholson and Blood Oath, all bourbon. defaultTypeName=bourbon since every named product is bourbon. Peat=none per American-bourbon norm (no peated malt used); not explicitly addressed on site.

Verified via producer's own site: Okinawan awamori distiller (Masahiro Shuzo) also producing whisky, a Pure Malt Whisky and a 12 Year Oloroso Sherry Cask expression plus a blended Kaijin release, tropical-fruit/vanilla profile, no smoke/peat. Confirms seed's identification; defaultTypeName left empty as range spans pure malt and blend.

MAJOR CORRECTION from seed (which found no web presence and guessed GB-SCT): Matt D'Arcy is a real historic Irish whiskey brand (Newry, Co. Down, est. 1817), revived by Echlinville Distillery (Co. Down, Northern Ireland) as a blend of 10-year-old grain whiskey and 17-year-old Irish single malt, Port-cask finished. Country coded IE per the marketed "Irish whiskey" category (no Northern-Ireland-specific code exists in the closed list). No peat/smoke mentioned; fruit/oak/spice profile.

Verified via producer's own site (muirheads-whisky.com/our-whisky): Muirhead's offers a Blue Seal (blended) range and a separate Silver Seal (Speyside single malt) range; this row covers Blue Seal. No peat/smoke in tasting notes. Search results indicated a 2008 acquisition by Terroir Distillers (also owner of Tullibardine), but that page would not render this session, so owner is left blank rather than asserted from an unopened source.

Identified: Muteki is a blended Japanese-style whisky bottled by Les Grands Chais de France (French drinks group); true distillation origin is undisclosed on the pages found, so countryCode is kept XX rather than asserted JP. Matured 3 years in sherry/bourbon casks plus a Mizunara finish. No peat/smoke mentioned (vanilla, ginger, citrus profile). Corrects seed's unknown/unverified status with a verified identity.

Re-verified directly: blended malt Scotch (malt only, no grain) from Glenturret, Highland Park and Macallan, owned by Edrington. Despite Highland Park being a peated contributor, the finished blend's own tasting notes (fudge, cooked apple, cherry) show no smoke, so peat=none for the finished product. Owner recorded as Edrington per this source; the seed's caveat that sibling brand Famous Grouse reportedly moved to William Grant & Sons in 2024/2025 could not be confirmed either way for Naked Grouse specifically and may need re-checking.

IDENTIFIED (seed could not find this brand, WebSearch budget exhausted): Noble Rebel is a Blended Malt Scotch Whisky range by Loch Lomond Group (Loch Lomond Distillery, Alexandria, Scotland; loch-lomond already live in the KB). Three named expressions: Orchard Outburst (unpeated, fruity/citrus -- this baseline row), Hazelnut Harmony, and Smoke Symphony (peated -- see rule.tsv, matched by name pattern since "Smoke Symphony" contains no literal "peat" keyword).

Verified: O'Brian is a triple-distilled blend of grain and malt distillates, marketed as Irish whiskey; produced/bottled by Fauconnier (est. 1829, part of La Martiniquaise since 2011), with blending/filtration stated to occur in France. Coded IE per the marketed "Irish whiskey" category (consistent with Irish-origin distillate under the GI, final blending/bottling in France being common practice). No peat/smoke mentioned. Corrects seed's GB-SCT guess -- this is not Scotch.

Identified via alcofan.com: Oakeshott is a blended Scotch whisky (15% single malt) produced by Glasgow Whisky Limited (est. 2007 by Graham Taylor and Stewart Hendry, Glasgow), sourcing malt/grain from Speyside and the Highlands. That source describes "a light peat component" / "light peatty smoke", but since it is a third-party retailer/blog rather than the producer's own domain (glasgowwhisky.com could not be confirmed this session to mention Oakeshott directly), peatProfile is left unknown rather than asserted -- withheld peat proposal: light, per https://alcofan.com/marka-viski-oakeshott.html.

Identified (seed found no web presence): Ogilhinn Nessia is a real Scotch whisky range, confirmed product "Ogilhinn Nessia Speyside Single Malt Whisky". Search results (whiskybase.com, Cloudflare-blocked this session so not independently opened) describe it as a bottler based in Scotland/UK with Speyside single malt and sherry-cask expressions, plus (per Ukrainian retailer listing snippets, not independently opened either) a "Choice" blend and "Storm"/"Cloud" single malts -- consistent with a multi-region own-label range, so kind is recorded as "brand" rather than "bottler" pending confirmation and region/defaultTypeName are left empty. The two catalogue sample names ("Highland Phantom Peak", "Speyside Celestia Creek") were not found verbatim anywhere on the web; they appear to be this same regionally-themed range under different specific bottlings. No peat evidence found, but the range is broad and unconfirmed, so kept unknown rather than none.

Verified via producer's own site: O.H. Ingram is the brand of The Ingram Distillery ("the only floating barrelhouse"), Columbus, Kentucky -- ages Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey aboard barges on the Mississippi River ("Mellowed on the Mississippi"). Flagship expressions include Flagship Bourbon and Single Barrel Captain's Choice (base spirit reported by third-party reviews to be distilled under contract at Green River Distillery, Owensboro, KY, then river-aged by Ingram). No peat/smoke; American bourbon norm. Corrects seed's low-confidence name-pattern guess with a verified identity; kind corrected from "blend" to "distillery".

Re-verified via producer's own site. Onikishi ("demon knight", 鬼侍) is a Blended Japanese Whisky owned by Milestone Beverages, a Hong Kong-headquartered brand developer/global distributor (portfolio also includes Mixology, Stateless, Taisteal, Blowfish, Atilius) -- no Japan-based distillery confirmed, so countryCode is corrected to XX rather than JP. CORRECTION: seed set peatProfile=light citing this same page's "cedar smoke" (Demon Knight finish) and "light smoky close" (Deadly Sakura finish) notes, but the producer's own copy attributes this to cedar/Mizunara-type cask aging, not peated malt -- cask-derived smoke is not peat (same distinction the KB draws for Jack Daniel's charcoal mellowing). peatProfile corrected to none; added flavor.tsv "smoky" (baseline, non-peat) instead.

Re-verified via producer's own site: vertically integrated single malt distillery in Rozelieures, Lorraine, France, run by the Grallet-Dupic family (6 generations); whisky production launched 2001 by Christophe Dupic. Base/core range (Rare Collection, Subtil Collection, Origine) is unpeated. Two separate peated lines confirmed on the producer's own site and added as rule.tsv rows since neither uses the English word "peat" (so the KB's generic "peated" keyword rule would not catch them): Tourbe (Tourbe Collection, own copy: peat "discreet/masked") and Fume (Fume Collection, own copy: "delicate" peat plus heavy ex-sherry cask char) -- both recorded as light.

Verified via producer's own site (corrects seed's "German-market brand" guess, whose two fetch attempts had failed): Ruotker's is the whiskey brand of Destillerie Golles, a family distillery in Riegersburg, AUSTRIA (distilling since 2003). Range includes Ruediger I/II (five-grain blend, matches sample "Ruotker's Ruediger"), Alois (rye finished in plum brandy cask), 100% Rye, 100% Corn aged in Oloroso Sherry cask (matches sample "Ruotker's Oloroso Sherry Cask"), Wilhelm (peated Scottish barley single malt) and a limited Peated Single Malt (PX sherry finish). Because the range spans both peated and unpeated expressions under one brand, the row's own peatProfile is kept unknown; the peated "Wilhelm" line is instead captured in rule.tsv (pattern-matched, since its name carries no peat keyword).

MAJOR CORRECTION from seed (which guessed Kentucky Straight Bourbon, US, unverified): Sam Barton is verified via its owner's own site (La Martiniquaise) to be an authentic CANADIAN whisky, made principally from rye, matured 5 years in Canadian oak. Floral/subtle/balanced profile; no peat/smoke mentioned, consistent with the North American norm.

Re-verified directly (seed's citation was accurate but marked low-confidence): Sazerac Rye is a rye whiskey brand of the Sazerac Company, distilled at Buffalo Trace Distillery, Frankfort, KY. No peat/smoke mentioned; American rye norm. Kind corrected from "blend" to "brand" since it is a straight rye product, not a blended-style whiskey. Upgraded to high confidence: the identity is directly verified even though the source does not explicitly state "unpeated" (peat left none per category norm, which this round's rules permit for a high-confidence row).

MAJOR CORRECTION from seed (which assumed "ordinary blended Scotch" by long-tail default policy): Scottish Deer is actually produced by MoldStandart, a MOLDOVAN spirits producer (cognacs, whisky, vodka -- portfolio also includes brands named "Irish Pub" and "WILSON"), explicitly described on its own product page as made "using Scottish technology" rather than actually being made in Scotland. Malt-barley single malt style, aged 3 years, 40% ABV, no peat/smoke mentioned. This is NOT a Scotch whisky despite the name.

Verified via producer's own site: unlike the similarly-named Scottish Deer elsewhere in this batch (which turned out to be Moldovan), Scottish Piper is a genuine blended Scotch whisky brand of Burlington Drinks (independent UK drinks company based near London; whiskies "aged in Scotland" per its own site). No peat/smoke mentioned; treated as an ordinary unpeated blend. The catalogue's two near-duplicate rows for this name remain covered by the one alias already on file.

Re-verified directly: "The Sexton Irish Whiskey" is confirmed a product of Proximo Spirits per Wikipedia's disambiguation page. Marketed as single malt Irish whiskey from an undisclosed source distillery. Kind corrected from "blend" to "brand": being single malt, it is definitionally not a blend, as the seed's own note already flagged as an awkward mapping. Peat=none per general Irish-whiskey category norm (no specific confirmation found).

IDENTIFIED (seed found no web presence): Shamrose Irish Whiskey is confirmed via the producer's own site as a line of Proud Irish Whiskey Company Ltd (Dublin, Ireland, est. 2015), a blend of 85% grain whiskey and 15% malt whiskey, triple distilled, matured in ex-bourbon American oak. No peat/smoke; sweetness/honey/caramel/fruit profile.

Re-verified via producer's own site: Skrewball is a peanut-butter-flavoured American whiskey founded 2018 by Steven and Brittany Yeng in Ocean Beach, San Diego, California; acquired by Pernod Ricard in 2023 (owner recorded as the current owner). Infused/flavoured product, not a traditional distillery; defaultTypeName left empty since none of the closed categories fit an infused whiskey. No peat/smoke; American whiskey base.
